topic.subject: chemistry
topic.title: Energy changes in reactions
topic.scopeBasis: TGS 2026-27 detailed outline only; not explicit in the 2025-26 Year 8 map
topic.overview: Chemical reactions transfer energy. Temperature observations, energy-level diagrams and bond-energy calculations help classify a reaction as exothermic or endothermic.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 scientific vocabulary and symbols.
Apply the idea to an unfamiliar example rather than relying on recognition.
Use the command word, show working where needed and include every mark point.
mustMemoriseRules: Exothermic reactions transfer energy to the surroundings, which usually warm up.
Endothermic reactions take in energy from the surroundings, which usually cool down.
In an exothermic profile products are at lower energy than reactants; in an endothermic profile products are higher.
Breaking bonds requires energy; making bonds releases energy.
Overall energy change = energy needed to break bonds - energy released making bonds.
Use insulated apparatus, equal quantities and the same starting temperature for fair temperature comparisons.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.meaning: transferring energy from the reacting system to the surroundings
taking in energy from the surroundings
everything outside the reacting system that can exchange energy with it
a diagram comparing energy of reactants and products
energy needed to break one mole of a specified bond in the model

workedExamples.prompt: Temperature rises from 20 C to 28 C. Classify.
workedExamples.answer: Exothermic: energy was transferred to the surroundings.

workedExamples.prompt: Bond breaking needs 600 kJ and bond making releases 750 kJ. Calculate change.

practicals.title: Compare temperature changes
practicals.aim: Classify reactions from measured temperature change.
practicals.variables: IV: reaction; DV: maximum/minimum temperature change; controls: volumes, concentrations, starting temperature and insulation.
practicals.method: Measure initial temperature, mix set quantities in an insulated cup, stir, record temperature frequently and calculate change; repeat.
practicals.expectedResult: A reliable rise indicates exothermic; a reliable fall indicates endothermic.
practicals.safety: Wear eye protection; use dilute reagents and a stable cup; follow reagent-specific controls.
practicals.evaluation: Use a lid and insulation, measure promptly with a probe, repeat and extrapolate cautiously if heat loss matters.

commonMistakes: Saying exothermic means the reactants contain no energy.
Reversing the signs in a bond-energy calculation.
Calling a reaction endothermic merely because it needed ignition.
examTips: State the direction of energy transfer, not only the temperature change.
On a profile, compare product and reactant energy levels.
Write break minus make before substituting values.
beforeStartingPractice: Read the key rules once, cover them, then retrieve them aloud or in writing.
Use MC first for confidence, but finish with typed, calculation, practical or explanation evidence.
After an error, study the explanation; the same concept returns later in a different format and again after 2 and 7 days.

practicals.subject: chemistry
practicals.title: Compare temperature changes
practicals.aim: Classify reactions from measured temperature change.
practicals.variables: IV: reaction; DV: maximum/minimum temperature change; controls: volumes, concentrations, starting temperature and insulation.
practicals.method: Measure initial temperature, mix set quantities in an insulated cup, stir, record temperature frequently and calculate change; repeat.
practicals.expectedResult: A reliable rise indicates exothermic; a reliable fall indicates endothermic.
practicals.safety: Wear eye protection; use dilute reagents and a stable cup; follow reagent-specific controls.
practicals.evaluation: Use a lid and insulation, measure promptly with a probe, repeat and extrapolate cautiously if heat loss matters.
